digo: Mchiza tsaka; Mwahula tsaka; Mngwa nyahi; Mnyinyi
digo_source: Pakia (2005) App. III; Pakia (2005) App. VI; Maundu & Tengnäs 2005 (Mchiza tsaka)

teaser.en: One of its Digo names means 'forest breaker', for the way it pushes up through the canopy and towers over the trees around it.

summary.en: *Mchiza tsaka* is a tall tree of dry evergreen coastal forest that rises above the canopy, with shining narrow leaves. It gives house poles, timber and firewood, and its leaves and roots are used in medicine.

about.en:
*Mchiza tsaka* is a tall tree, up to 24 metres, with a straight, slightly buttressed trunk and smooth grey bark. Its leaves are narrow and shiny.

The fruits are unusual: clusters of slender, pod-like arms that radiate from a single point, red and green, like a small bunch of fingers. They belong to the custard-apple family, and their seeds are typical of it.

where.en: It grows in dry evergreen forest on coral rag and sand, the kind of forest found in the kayas and remnant coastal forests of the south coast. Its crown often stands higher than the trees around it.

uses.en: Its straight stems are used as house-building poles, and the wood gives timber and firewood. The leaves and roots are used in medicine.

culture.en: Its many Digo names describe it closely. *Mchiza tsaka* means it 'overgrows the forest', and *mwahula tsaka* means 'forest breaker', both for the way it tops the canopy. *Mnyinyi* refers to its shining leaves.

names.en: Pakia records four Digo names: *mchiza tsaka*, *mwahula tsaka*, *mngwa nyahi* and *mnyinyi*; Maundu and Tengnäs also give *mchiza tsaka*. In Giriama it is *mbarawa* or *mukuna mbawa*. No Swahili or common English name has been recorded; its scientific name is *Xylopia parviflora*.

reason.en: Same family (Annonaceae), a coastal forest tree
Same family: the wild custard apple

sources: Pakia, M. (2005) African Traditional Plant Knowledge Today: an ethnobotanical study of the Digo at the Kenya Coast. PhD thesis, Univ. Bayreuth, Appendix III (Digo–botanical name list) & Appendix VI (name semantics). https://epub.uni-bayreuth.de/881/1/Pakia.pdf
